title: Choosing flowers
statementMd:
Vladimir would like to prepare a present for his wife: they have an anniversary! He decided to buy her **exactly** $n$ flowers.

Vladimir went to a flower shop, and he was amazed to see that there are $m$ types of flowers being sold there, and there is unlimited supply of flowers of each type. Vladimir wants to choose flowers to maximize the happiness of his wife. He knows that after receiving the first flower of the $i$-th type happiness of his wife increases by $a_i$ and after receiving each consecutive flower of this type her happiness increases by $b_i$. That is, if among the chosen flowers there are $x_i \gt 0$ flowers of type $i$, his wife gets $a_i + (x_i - 1) \cdot b_i$ additional happiness (and if there are no flowers of type $i$, she gets nothing for this particular type).

Please help Vladimir to choose exactly $n$ flowers to maximize the total happiness of his wife.

## Input

The first line contains the only integer $t$ ($1 \leq t \leq 10\,000$), the number of test cases. It is followed by $t$ descriptions of the test cases.

Each test case description starts with two integers $n$ and $m$ ($1 \le n \le 10^9$, $1 \le m \le 100\,000$), the number of flowers Vladimir needs to choose and the number of types of available flowers.

The following $m$ lines describe the types of flowers: each line contains integers $a_i$ and $b_i$ ($0 \le a_i, b_i \le 10^9$) for $i$-th available type of flowers.

The test cases are separated by a blank line. It is guaranteed that the sum of values $m$ among all test cases does not exceed $100\,000$.

## Output

For each test case output a single integer: the maximum total happiness of Vladimir's wife after choosing exactly $n$ flowers optimally.

## Note

In the first example case Vladimir can pick 1 flower of the first type and 3 flowers of the second type, in this case the total happiness equals $5 + (1 + 2 \cdot 4) = 14$.

In the second example Vladimir can pick 2 flowers of the first type, 2 flowers of the second type, and 1 flower of the third type, in this case the total happiness equals $(5 + 1 \cdot 2) + (4 + 1 \cdot 2) + 3 = 16$.
statementZhMd:
弗拉基米尔想为妻子准备一份礼物：他们的结婚纪念日到了！他决定购买 **恰好** $n$ 朵花。

弗拉基米尔来到一家花店，惊讶地发现那里出售 $m$ 种花，并且每种花的供应都是无限的。弗拉基米尔希望选择花朵，使妻子获得的幸福感最大。他知道，妻子收到第 $i$ 种花的第一朵时，幸福感会增加 $a_i$；之后每收到一朵这种花，幸福感会增加 $b_i$。也就是说，如果所选花朵中有 $x_i \gt 0$ 朵第 $i$ 种花，那么妻子会因此获得 $a_i + (x_i - 1) \cdot b_i$ 的额外幸福感（如果没有选择第 $i$ 种花，则不会因这种花获得幸福感）。

请帮助弗拉基米尔选择恰好 $n$ 朵花，使妻子的幸福感总和最大。

## 输入格式

第一行包含一个整数 $t$（$1 \leq t \leq 10\,000$），表示测试用例的数量。接下来是 $t$ 个测试用例的描述。

每个测试用例的描述首先包含两个整数 $n$ 和 $m$（$1 \leq n \leq 10^9$，$1 \leq m \leq 100\,000$），分别表示弗拉基米尔需要选择的花朵数量和可选花朵的种类数。

接下来的 $m$ 行描述花朵的种类：每行包含两个整数 $a_i$ 和 $b_i$（$0 \leq a_i, b_i \leq 10^9$），表示第 $i$ 种可选花朵的相关数值。

测试用例之间用空行分隔。保证所有测试用例的 $m$ 之和不超过 $100\,000$。

## 输出格式

对于每个测试用例，输出一个整数：以最优方式选择恰好 $n$ 朵花后，弗拉基米尔的妻子能够获得的最大幸福感总和。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，弗拉基米尔可以选择第 1 种花 1 朵、第 2 种花 3 朵，此时幸福感总和为 $5 + (1 + 2 \cdot 4) = 14$。

在第二个样例中，弗拉基米尔可以选择第 1 种花 2 朵、第 2 种花 2 朵、第 3 种花 1 朵，此时幸福感总和为 $(5 + 1 \cdot 2) + (4 + 1 \cdot 2) + 3 = 16$。
